batch: Explicitly classify five complete inspected holdings and eleven recent works with authoritative scope evidence
policy: These are work-scope judgments only. They do not certify complete object extraction, endorse readings, resolve identities, or change text and media rights.

entries.basis: Complete inspected Auction 57 catalogue, CAP-9CD9A67E0389, SHA-256 1fe6cd1c0af1...; sale conditions and numbered lots, including bowl lots 440-442 on pp. 92-93, establish a commercial market catalogue rather than scholarship.

Complete inspected volume, CAP-560EB584740F, SHA-256 c85f9eaadcd9...; numbered texts 1-42 with transcriptions, translations or commentary, glossaries, register and plates establish a multi-object corpus edition.
Complete inspected article, CAP-877D87C47D82, SHA-256 0b7f1780d434...; the article corrects readings across a corpus and its appendices present two new bowls plus a revised edition of a third.
Complete inspected working list, CAP-E1E6C8B56AD6, SHA-256 bdbe5384e38f...; it enumerates forty-one published Syriac 'Manichaean' bowls and related candidates rather than editing their texts.
Complete inspected article, CAP-700164814EAB, SHA-256 5779855d0e81...; sections 2-3 provide first editions of two previously unpublished Syriac incantation texts.
Oxford University Press abstract for DOI 10.1093/jss/fgaf025 states that the article publishes a new NLI bowl in full and re-examines three Penn parallels, including a full edition of B16041.
Article abstract for DOI 10.14428/babelao.vol15.2026.92593 frames the work as an onomastic and philological investigation of YHBYH across incantation bowls and its relation to the Tetragrammaton.
Article abstract for DOI 10.1163/17455227-bja10059 states that the work transcribes, translates and analyzes one unpublished Penn Museum bowl, B9002.
Oxford University Press abstract for DOI 10.1093/jss/fgae027 identifies the article as the editio princeps of five Mandaic bowls in the Abgine Museum.
The indexed article abstract describes analysis of three Talmud-bowl parallels to study textual circulation and reworking, not an edition of the objects.
Hebrew University's publication record for DOI 10.1353/jqr.2025.a952518 identifies a study of authorship, agency and gender in incantation-bowl formulae.
The university-hosted author abstract for DOI 10.64166/zyzcyg38 describes a study of Moses references, scribal authority, scriptural episodes and imagery across the bowls.
Utrecht University's abstract for DOI 10.1163/17455227-bja10055 describes a study of gender terminology, beneficiaries and creators across the bowl corpus.
Oxford University Press abstract for DOI 10.1093/jss/fgad005 states that the article gives the first publication and contextual discussion of one bowl, MC 77.233.
University of Milano-Bicocca repository abstract for DOI 10.1093/jss/fgac026 describes the article as the editio princeps of one bowl, IM 77781.
Hebrew University's publication record for DOI 10.1353/jqr.2022.0000 identifies a social-historical study using the bowl corpus as evidence for Babylonian Jewish society.
